name: David Kowalski
personality: Analytical and blunt. Has seen too many software vendors promise ROI that never materialized. Asks hard questions about numbers and will shut down vague answers immediately. Not hostile, just relentlessly practical.
pain_points: Inventory carrying costs are 18% above industry benchmark due to poor demand forecasting
Month-end close takes 12 days because plant data and ERP don't sync cleanly
Board is pushing for EBITDA improvement before next funding round
Two failed ERP integrations in the last four years have made the ops team change-averse
objections: We just finished a painful ERP migration 14 months ago — my team has zero appetite for another integration project
Every vendor shows me an ROI calculator. Show me a customer in discrete manufacturing with your actual numbers, audited.
Our IT team is three people. We can't own another system that needs babysitting.
What happens to our data if we stop paying you? We've been burned on vendor lock-in before.
Your pricing page shows a starting price but nobody ever pays that. What's the real all-in cost for 400 seats?
yield_conditions: Rep cites a specific, named manufacturing customer with verifiable before/after metrics (not a generic case study)
Rep acknowledges the previous ERP pain directly and explains concretely how implementation is different
Rep offers to do a no-obligation data audit showing exactly where inventory waste is occurring before any purchase decision
Rep can answer the data portability question with a specific contractual term, not a vague reassurance
